no-0DaH.title: Landscape: vast grassy fields, round rock walls
no-0DaH.summary: Farmland south of Stavanger is flat, with vast open fields of grass rather than crops, and walls built from large round rocks.

no-0MXz.title: Bollard: thin curved, black parallelogram
no-0MXz.summary: A thin, curved rectangular bollard with the reflector inside a black parallelogram.

no-0UKk.title: Speed sign: white sign saying "Sone"
no-0UKk.summary: White signs that say "Sone", usually with a speed limit, are common in towns.

no-0YsK.title: Street sign: centred on top of the post
no-0YsK.summary: Street name signs are mounted centred on top of sign posts. In Sweden they are fixed to the side of posts or lamp posts.

differs.how: Signs are fixed to the side of posts or lamp posts

no-0l1i.title: Language: Russian beside local on signs
no-0l1i.summary: Russian sometimes appears next to Norwegian on signs near the Russian border, mostly on the E6 and E105 near Kirkenes.

no-4foM.title: Sign: bilingual with Sámi letters Á and Đ
no-4foM.summary: Some northern signs are in two languages with Sámi, which has letters like Á and Đ and many vowels in a row. Not all signs there are bilingual.

no-6F9C.title: Snow pole: thin wooden with painted reflector
no-6F9C.summary: Thin wooden snow poles with painted reflectors are fairly common. In other Nordic countries wooden ones usually have no reflector.

no-7dqj.title: Landscape: very flat farmland
no-7dqj.summary: The biggest farmland area, around Oslo, is much flatter than most of the country, with smooth round forested hills in the distance. The area southeast of Oslo is the flattest.

no-8i89.title: Lamp posts: two red stripes
no-8i89.summary: Two red stripes around lamp posts are common in the southwestern city of Stavanger.

no-9ScA.title: Pole plate: small wide black, one line of text
no-9ScA.summary: Small, wide black pole plates with a single line of letters and numbers are found in the southeast.

no-9ybH.hide: no learnable content (points to a separate guide)

no-A0UC.title: Plate: long white, green for vans
no-A0UC.summary: Long white plates with the European strip on the left. Commercial vehicles, often vans, have green plates. In Europe green plates are most common here but also appear on electric vehicles elsewhere.

no-A94U.title: Landscape: rolling land, tiny birches
no-A94U.summary: The northeast has rolling land instead of tall mountains, with very small birches and patchy grass.

no-FI4P.title: Sign: four bolts in a tall rectangle
no-FI4P.summary: Most small road signs are fixed with four visible bolts in a tall rectangle. Framed signs also appear sometimes, mostly in towns.

no-FTW1.title: Trees: spruce in the southern half
no-FTW1.summary: Spruces grow mainly in the southern half, especially in the southeast and around Trondheim.

no-HH6f.title: Vegetation: coastal grassland
no-HH6f.summary: Coastal grassland with hardly any other plants and low, distant mountains is found on coastal roads in the far north.

no-HfAL.title: Plants: tall bracken fern in the south
no-HfAL.summary: Bracken has a fairly tall stem with many wide leaves, and grows mostly in the south. Other ferns grow further north.

no-HlLb.title: Sign: blue sign with large white M
no-HlLb.summary: Small roads often have blue signs with a large white M. Sweden has similar signs, but its M's middle point does not reach the bottom. Finland has none.

differs.how: The M's middle point stops above the bottom
Has no such signs

no-HrQE.title: Route marker: first digit shows the region
no-HrQE.summary: The first digit of road numbers depends on the region, with some exceptions among one- and two-digit roads. A few roads start with 9. Regional "Fv" roads don't follow the pattern.

no-IYC5.title: Sign: bright yellow roadworks signs
no-IYC5.summary: Road construction signs have a bright yellow background.

no-Iw1G.title: Landscape: sharp rocky peaks, few trees
no-Iw1G.summary: Sharp, rocky mountains with few trees are typical of the Lofoten islands.

no-JxsR.title: Road lines: long dashed edges, yellow centre
no-JxsR.summary: Small roads have long dashed white edge lines. Larger roads have solid edges and an orange-tinted yellow middle line. Sweden has shorter dashes and only white lines, Finland has solid edges.

differs.how: Edge dashes are shorter, only white lines
Solid edge lines, centre line yellow or white

no-Leu7.title: Landscape: very hilly farmland, steep and uneven
no-Leu7.summary: Farmland around Trondheim is very hilly, with hills steeper and more uneven than in the southeast.

no-MAXX.title: Direction sign: yellow with black border
no-MAXX.summary: Direction signs are yellow with a black border. The road number sits in a green box for European and major roads, or a white box for smaller roads.

no-NRTp.title: Pole plate: fairly large, black or red
no-NRTp.summary: Fairly large black or red plates on poles are found in the capital.

no-O5ze.title: Guardrail: wooden posts
no-O5ze.summary: Guardrails often have wooden posts, which is uncommon in Sweden and Finland.

differs.how: Wooden posts are uncommon
Wooden posts are uncommon

no-OM8Z.title: Plants: brightly coloured moss
no-OM8Z.summary: Brightly coloured moss is common between Lillehammer and Oppdal.

no-OjhH.title: Houses: wooden, red or black, many white
no-OjhH.summary: Nearly all houses are wooden. Many are red, and black ones are more common than in Sweden or Finland. Norway has more white houses and fewer brick or yellow ones.

differs.how: More red and yellow houses, more brick
More red and yellow houses, more brick

no-Oub6.title: Trees: oak in the far south
no-Oub6.summary: Oaks grow mainly in the far south.

no-RLu2.title: Trees: pine on the coast and far inland
no-RLu2.summary: Pines are most common on the coast and in far inland areas of the southern half.

no-SSKX.title: Pole: lamp fixed with one thick bolt
no-SSKX.summary: Lamps on wooden poles are held by one thick bolting. Sweden and Finland use a double bolting.

differs.how: Double bolting
Double bolting

no-TPpp.title: Landscape: very mountainous with fjords
no-TPpp.summary: Very mountainous, with fjords along most of the coast. Finland and Denmark are mostly flat, and Sweden is a mix of flat, hilly and mountainous.

differs.how: Mix of flat, hilly and mountainous land
Mostly flat
Mostly flat

no-VlO3.title: Snow pole: black plastic
no-VlO3.summary: Black plastic snow poles are regional, most common between Bergen and Trondheim (mostly the west and central areas) and less often elsewhere.

no-W3mj.title: Houses: all-white wooden villages
no-W3mj.summary: White wooden houses exist everywhere, but whole villages of them are especially common on the south coast.

no-Yvvo.title: Snow pole: orange, thin white reflector mid-pole
no-Yvvo.summary: Orange snow poles with a fairly thin white reflector near the middle of the pole. Swedish ones have a wider reflector set higher up.

differs.how: Wider reflector set higher on the pole

no-Yy1U.title: Chevron: yellow on black
no-Yy1U.summary: Curve chevrons are yellow arrows on black.

no-c3nG.title: Guardrail: rusty
no-c3nG.summary: Rusty guardrails are almost only found in coastal areas, especially the southern half of the west coast.

no-cISF.title: Trees: maple near southern farmland
no-cISF.summary: Maples grow mainly in the south, especially by the farmland around Oslo.

no-dZk6.title: Street sign: names ending in -vei or -gate
no-dZk6.summary: The most common street name endings are vei and gate, joined to the name as -veien or -gata.

no-hBEv.title: Vegetation: barren highland, no trees or bushes
no-hBEv.summary: Barren highlands with no trees or bushes, often with rocky mountains by the road, are mostly in the southwest.

no-hUl3.title: Bus stop sign: small blue with a white bus
no-hUl3.summary: Bus stops usually have a small blue sign with a white bus. Sweden has many bus stop styles but none like this.

differs.how: No bus stop sign like this

no-hWzL.title: Sign: pedestrian crossing, four stripes
no-hWzL.summary: A crossing sign with four stripes and a very simple drawn person. A five-stripe version and a version with a hat also exist. Finland has five stripes, Sweden four stripes but a more detailed person.

differs.how: Four stripes but a detailed person without a hat
Five stripes
Four stripes too, but not the bold simple person

no-jmxl.title: Houses: grass-covered roofs
no-jmxl.summary: Traditional houses often have grass-covered roofs, which is much less common in Sweden and Finland.

differs.how: Far less common
Far less common

no-lXDj.title: Houses: densely built old wooden town
no-lXDj.summary: The old mining town of Røros has densely packed traditional wooden buildings.

no-lm-3313.title: Bus: company name "Snelandia"
no-lm-3313.summary: Buses in the far north county of Finnmark are run by a company called Snelandia.

no-lm-3314.title: Bus: blue diamond logo with a small t
no-lm-3314.summary: Buses in Troms use a blue diamond-shaped logo with a lowercase t.

no-lm-3319.title: Bus: brand name "FRAMMR"
no-lm-3319.summary: Buses in Møre og Romsdal use the FRAMMR brand.

no-lm-3320.title: Bus: brand name "Skyss"
no-lm-3320.summary: Buses in Vestland use the Skyss brand.

no-lm-3321.title: Bus: green swoosh logo
no-lm-3321.summary: Buses in Vestfold use a distinct green swoosh-shaped logo.

no-lm-3322.title: Bus: dual "Nordland" and "Reis" logos
no-lm-3322.summary: Buses in Nordland carry two brands, Nordland and Reis.

no-lm-3323.title: Bus: "AtB" logo
no-lm-3323.summary: Buses in Trøndelag use the AtB brand.

no-lm-3324.title: Bus: green ">" shaped logo
no-lm-3324.summary: Buses in Rogaland are Kolumbus, with a green greater-than-sign logo.

no-lm-3325.title: Bus: brand name "Farte"
no-lm-3325.summary: Buses in Telemark use the Farte brand, a name that is easy to remember in English.

no-lm-3326.title: Bus: green circular "A" logo
no-lm-3326.summary: The Agder bus company has a green circular A logo.

no-lm-3327.title: Bus: brand name "Brakar"
no-lm-3327.summary: Buses in Buskerud are Brakar, with the logo shown.

no-lm-3328.title: Bus: brand name "Innlandstrafikk"
no-lm-3328.summary: The bus company in Innlandet is called Innlandstrafikk.

no-lm-3329.title: Bus: brand name "Ruter" with # symbol
no-lm-3329.summary: Buses around the capital are Ruter. The most distinctive part is the hashtag symbol that is always shown.

no-lm-7742.title: Snow pole: bamboo
no-lm-7742.summary: Bamboo snow poles are regional, mostly in the inland and east-central counties, and rarely in the west and south.

no-lm-7743.title: Snow pole: small and blue
no-lm-7743.summary: Small blue snow poles are found around the town of Elverum.

no-lm-7744.title: Snow pole: green plastic
no-lm-7744.summary: Green plastic snow poles are found mostly around the island of Senja in Troms, where the seller is based, and less often across Troms and Finnmark.

no-lm-7745.title: Snow pole: big wooden sticks
no-lm-7745.summary: Big wooden sticks mark roads that stay snowy almost all year, such as north of Hardangervidda, west of Jotunheimen and southwest of Valdres.

no-lm-7746.title: Road: thick snow beside a skinny road
no-lm-7746.summary: A skinny road with about 1 metre of thick snow beside it and no trees. This is the road between Aadneram and Nomeland.

no-lm-7747.title: Road: flat, tabletop hill, short scrub
no-lm-7747.summary: A flat road with one hill shaped like a table, short scrub along the road and often water in view, on an island in the far north.

no-lm-7748.title: Road: very green, big treeless mountains
no-lm-7748.summary: A very green road with big mountains that have no trees. Right at the Swedish border there are parts without trees.

no-lm-7749.title: Road: huge mountains, skinny, bridges
no-lm-7749.summary: A skinny road with huge mountains, water to the east, many bridges and open tunnels, fireweed along the sides and yellowish vegetation.

no-lm-7750.title: Road: valley with treeless mountain range
no-lm-7750.summary: A road through a valley with a big mountain range without trees alongside, some very green parts and some with fireweed.

no-lm-7751.title: Road: very windy and skinny with 28 hairpins
no-lm-7751.summary: A very windy, skinny road with 28 hairpin turns down a mountain. Big power lines, huge mountains in the distance and very cloudy coverage.

no-lm-7752.title: Road: no trees, small white rocks
no-lm-7752.summary: A famous road with no trees and small white rocks, with fairly low visibility. Some parts are flat, others have small hills and lakes.

no-lm-7753.title: Road: dark-rock bridges, water on both sides
no-lm-7753.summary: A road using dark rocks as bridges, with water on both sides and dark clouds. It includes a famous bridge.

no-lm-7754.title: Coverage: flat island, Gen 2, lots of boats
no-lm-7754.summary: A flat island with only old Gen 2 coverage and lots of boats everywhere.

no-lm-7755.title: Road: very steep, windy, dark rock with moss
no-lm-7755.summary: A road down a huge mountain, very steep and windy, with very dark rock and green moss. Some parts are cut into the rock, with waterfalls.

no-lm-7756.title: Coverage: road completely covered in snow
no-lm-7756.summary: The road between Atna and Ringebu is fully covered in snow, a winter scene with green rocks.

no-oDKo.title: Sign: red outline on white background
no-oDKo.summary: Traffic signs have a red outline and a white background. Swedish and Finnish ones have a yellow background.

differs.how: Yellow background
Yellow background

no-p8gR.title: Fire hydrant: specific green design
no-p8gR.summary: A particular green fire hydrant design is found in the west coast city of Bergen.

no-qjon.title: Pole: wooden with small black metal cap
no-qjon.summary: Wooden poles, often with a small black metal cap on top. Sweden and Finland have this cap too.

no-raUu.title: Route marker: small white square sign
no-raUu.summary: Small white square signs showing the road number and the distance to the nearest town are common on medium roads. The number starts with R or F. F roads are hard to locate, R roads are easier.

no-u4g0.title: Language: Æ, Ø and Å, "kk" spelling
no-u4g0.summary: Norwegian uses Æ, Ø and Å, the same as Danish. Swedish has Å but not Æ or Ø and spells with "ck" where Norwegian uses "kk".

differs.how: Has Å but no Æ or Ø, and spells "ck"

no-wQZ6.title: Coverage: humid green road, overcast
no-wQZ6.summary: Near the Russian border the road looks humid and green with very overcast, sometimes foggy coverage. Trees are fairly low, mostly thin birches and pines.

no-x2Iy.title: Google car: low smallcam, wide round blur
no-x2Iy.summary: The newer Gen 4 smallcam sits lower than normal with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. It can be see-through. Most of Northern Europe has it.

no-x4nu.title: Landscape: big farmland in three areas
no-x4nu.summary: Large farmland is found in only three areas: the southeast, around Trondheim and south of Stavanger. The next clues tell them apart.

no-xAUQ.title: Landscape: deep fjords, tall mountains
no-xAUQ.summary: Deep fjords with tall mountains around them are most common between Bergen and Trondheim.

no-xl0F.title: Landscape: bare rock with small coastal pines
no-xl0F.summary: Exposed rock, often dotted with small coastal pines and bushes, is mainly on the south coast.

no-zQPw.title: Road lines: made of small dots of paint
no-zQPw.summary: Road lines are often made of small dots of paint rather than smooth paint.
